subject: Post-demo: deployment path & latency/throughput qualifiers
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Tom Nguyen <tom@fastretail.com>, Elena Rios <elena@fastretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-12T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo: deployment path & latency/throughput qualifiers

Thanks again for the demo time today — appreciate you walking through the checkout and personalization flows. Quick recap from our side and three clarifying asks so we can firm up a recommendation (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private).

Summary of what we heard (please correct if I got anything wrong):
- P95 tail requirement: checkout confirmation path: target <= 120 ms; personalization suggestions: target <= 250 ms.
- Average prompt length: ~55 tokens (user prompt + metadata); worst-case prompt ~220 tokens.
- Current concurrent steady QPS: 80–120 for checkout (EU/US split 60/40); daily peak bursts up to ~360 QPS for ~8–12 minutes during sale windows.
- Data residency: primary US, EU-sensitive customer segments later this year.
- SLO sensitivity: any 200+ ms regression on checkout path likely needs mitigation/fallbacks.

Three asks so we can recommend a path:
1) Can you share a 48-hour traffic sample (timestamps + request sizes) or a small CSV of QPS buckets so we can model batching behavior?
2) Do you have an internal SLA/cost target per 1M tokens? This helps balance hosted cost vs reserved (Dedicated) commit.
3) Are there upcoming regulatory customers that would require a VPC/on-prem evaluation in next 6 months?

Initial read: Given a hard 120 ms P95 on checkout plus frequent short bursts to 360 QPS, Dedicated capacity looks likely for predictable latency. Hosted might work with aggressive routing + higher-tier capacity if you can accept modest tail risk and implement a cheap fallback. Private (VPC) only necessary if regulatory or on-prem data controls are mandatory.

Next steps I propose:
- You drop the traffic sample (ask #1) — I’ll run a latency-throughput simulation and return a short matrix (hosted vs dedicated cost/latency tradeoffs).
- Marissa will share a pilot ZIP (pricing + terms) and Ben will propose a benchmark slot.

Attaching a simple throughput profile CSV template I mentioned.

Thanks,
Jonas
Sr. Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachment: throughput_profile_v2.csv (stub)

From: Tom Nguyen <tom@fastretail.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Rios <elena@fastretail.com>
Date: 2026-10-12T17:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: deployment path & latency/throughput qualifiers

Thanks Jonas — this is helpful. A few clarifications inline: 

- Checkout P95: yes, sub-120 ms is our goal for desktop/mobile client confirmation flows (we can tolerate occasional spikes to ~160ms but not sustained).
- Personalization target: ~200 ms P95 would be fine.
- Prompt sizes: 50–70 tokens typical; 200+ only for diagnostic/admin prompts (rare).
- Traffic sample: I asked our infra team to export 72 hours of request logs — I'll send the CSV by EOD tomorrow (contains timestamp, endpoint, token_count).
- Cost: we are still finalizing internal economics; current guardrail is ~$300–400 per 1M tokens (not public), but we expect to negotiate pilot pricing.
- Compliance: no on-prem mandate this quarter; possibility of EU-only tenancy next year for a subset of data.

We are interested in a fast pilot to validate latency under real traffic — ideally a week-long dedicated pilot with a canary routing to Hosted for overflow. Can you outline what that looks like and any prerequisites? Also Marissa, looping you in on timing and procurement next steps.

—Tom
Head of Platform
FastRetail

Date: 2026-10-13T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: deployment path & latency/throughput qualifiers

Perfect — thanks for the fast reply and for requesting the logs. Quick answers to the pilot ask and prerequisites: 

Pilot outline (week-long dedicated pilot):
- Provision a temporary Dedicated pool sized for your peak burst profile (we can oversubscribe to avoid cold starts).
- Canary routing: 90% traffic to Dedicated, 10% overflow to Hosted with deterministic fallback.
- Benchmark plan: Ben will run a 1-hour synthetic run with your 72-hour real traffic replay plus a 30-minute stress burst at 120% peak.
- Observability: token-level cost, p95/p99 latency dashboards, KV cache hit rates.

Prereqs from FastRetail:
1) The 72-hour CSV (timestamp, endpoint, token_count) — you'll send this.
2) API key & CIDR ranges for the pilot (if you want IP-restricted ingress).
3) Decision on whether EU-only tenancy is required for the pilot (defaults to multi-region US with EU fallback).

I'll start the sizing model once I have the CSV — expected deliverable back to you within 48 hours: a short matrix that shows expected p95 by route for Hosted vs Dedicated, and an estimated per-day cost for the pilot.

Looping Ben so he can propose exact benchmark times.

Thanks,
Jonas
